public_rationale: On a plain reading, 'barely approximated a thing that society wanted' is a claim about demand. OpenAI said in March 2025, two months before the post, that 500 million people used ChatGPT every week. That is very broad voluntary use. A later NBER paper, partly by OpenAI staff, found that most ChatGPT messages are not work-related. That cuts against the claim's one exception, businesses replacing paid work more cheaply. Whether society 'needed' LLMs is a value judgment I do not score. The demand part, which carries the claim, is contradicted.
limitations: User counts come from OpenAI itself.
Free use may overstate value, and 'needed' is normative.
The verdict depends on reading 'wanted' as revealed demand.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs could generate a lot of text or pictures, which barely approximated anything society wanted or needed, other than being something people used to be willing to pay more for.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: from ChatGPT's launch to the post, there was little real demand for LLM output, apart from businesses wanting cheaper substitutes for paid human work.
I measure 'wanted' by revealed demand: how many people chose to use LLM products, and for what. 'Needed' is normative, so I do not test it separately.
Target period: November 2022 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Usage of LLM products by the public stayed small, or was mostly businesses replacing paid work.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Hundreds of millions of people chose to use LLM products regularly, including a large share of personal, non-work use, before the post.
